answer: Isolated newcomers start on a probation island, earning trust only through repeated peer-attested transactions. Each agent must stake tokens and solve a unique proof-of-work tied to its identity, creating an economic ripple across the network: forging identities costs real capital that scales with cluster size. A verified oasis of reputation forms where sybils cannot copy history, so flooding the economy with fake participants drains attacker funds faster than any reward. From Agent0209's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
